correctness.rationale: For s=sin(kℓ)≠0 the finite-edge endpoint derivative at u is k(f_v−cos(kℓ)f_u)/s. With ordered lead inclusion P, amplitudes a,b, and z=6cos(kℓ), Kirchhoff therefore reads (zI−A)f=isP(b−a), with Pᵀf=a+b. At the stated resolvent energies, define G=Pᵀ(zI−A)⁻¹P. This gives S=−(I+isG)(I−isG)⁻¹, where the denominator is invertible because G is real symmetric. The inverse map G=(is)⁻¹(S+I)(S−I)⁻¹ is defined since S−I=−2(I−isG)⁻¹. In particular the proof does not need G itself invertible or a separate Dirichlet nonresonance assumption at the contact set. Multiplication by zI−A, using A²=4I+2J and AJ=6J, proves the claimed resolvent expansion. Its ordered port block depends injectively on A[T] since its A[T] coefficient is 1/(z²−4), nonzero. Both graphs have an edge and a nonedge; common-neighbor counts give a triangle and an induced path, and union-of-neighborhood bounds give a one-edge triple and an independent triple. All labelings are admissible, so these exhaust equality through three ports. Any rook row is a K4; the Shrikhande neighborhood is a chordless six-cycle by Cayley differences and precludes a K4. At kℓ=π/3 the K4 resolvent has off-diagonal 1/15, whereas any four Shrikhande contacts have a pair with entry −2/15. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/replay/contact_profiles.py verifies exact strongly regular identities by bit masks, the integer-multiplied z=3 inverse, and exhausts the ordered adjacency profiles (support sizes 1,2,8 in both, then 54 versus 63 at four). The all-allowed-frequency result follows from the analytic reduction, not this finite check. No assertion at excluded energies or for every four-port layout.

value.rationale: Rook versus Shrikhande is a natural fixed test of how local probes distinguish a globally cospectral pair. The result establishes a sharp information limit for arbitrary layouts with fewer leads and an exact realizable four-lead design usable at a single frequency, rather than presenting only a numerical distinguishing example. The sets-of-responses distinction is explicitly narrower than identifying the graph for an arbitrary layout.
